 Galveston County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0019
 Vincent Bryant, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Plaintiff's Original Petition
Filed:
June 13, 2024
Plaintiff's counsel:
Colleen Orr, Conley & Stephenson Law Group
PARTIES
Plaintiff Vincent Bryant is an individual residing in Texas who was the driver of a vehicle involved in the collision described
below. Defendant is an automobile insurance carrier authorized to transact business in the State of Texas, which issued the policy
under which Plaintiff seeks benefits and against which this claim is brought.
FACTS
On February 11, 2024, Plaintiff was traveling lawfully in Pasadena when another vehicle crossed into Plaintiff's lane and struck
Plaintiff's vehicle head-on. The impact occurred at a low rate of speed, but it was sufficient to force Plaintiff's head and neck
forward and then back against the seat and headrest. Plaintiff reported the collision to the police and to Defendant, and Plaintiff
has cooperated fully with the claim investigation. Defendant was notified of the claim and has not paid the benefits owed under
the policy in a timely manner.
NEGLIGENCE
The at-fault driver failed to keep a proper lookout, failed to control the vehicle, and drove into the oncoming lane. Defendant, as
the insurer responsible for the policy benefits, owed Plaintiff a duty to investigate the claim promptly and fairly, to evaluate it in
good faith, and to pay covered amounts once liability and damages were reasonably clear. Defendant breached those duties by
delaying evaluation and failing to tender payment within a reasonable time, in violation of the Texas Insurance Code and
applicable Texas law on unfair claim settlement practices.
DAMAGES
As a direct result of the collision, Plaintiff sustained a neck strain that has caused pain, stiffness, headaches, and limited range of
motion. Plaintiff has incurred medical expenses for examination and treatment, lost time from work, and suffered physical pain
and mental anguish. Plaintiff seeks recovery of policy benefits, statutory interest, reasonable attorney's fees, and court costs, and
seeks total damages in the amount of $200,000.00.
